newsitem.title: USA: US manufacturing chief warns of danger of dlr rise.
newsitem.headline: US manufacturing chief warns of danger of dlr rise.

text.p: The head of the National Association of Manufacturers voiced concern on Tuesday about the recent strength of the dollar and said that another five to 10 percent rise in the currency would be a serious problem.

"The stronger the dollar goes, the more difficult it is to sell our products overseas," NAM Chairman Warren Batts told Reuters Financial Television. "Another five or 10 percent and we'd be in serious trouble."

"We're concerned about it (the dollar) getting out of line," Batts, who is also chairman of Tupperware Corp and Premark International, said. "If it keeps strengthening the way it is going, it will have an effect on us."
Turning to the domestic economy, Batts said the jobless rate cannot fall much further without hurting the economy.

"I don't think unemployment can go a great deal lower without something beginning to give," he said. "But if we're correct and the economy is going to slow a bit, I don't think unemployment is going to go down a significant number."
The unemployment rate now stands at 5.2 percent.
